function Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $CimProcess
    )

    if (-not [string]::Equals(
        [string]$CimProcess.ExecutablePath,
        [string]$K3Tunnel.SshExe,
        [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )) {
        return $false
    }

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {
        return $false
    }

    $requiredText = @(
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
        ) -lt 0) {
            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {
    $processes = @(
        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
            -Filter "Name='ssh.exe'" `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    foreach ($process in $processes) {
        if (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $process) {
            $process
        }
    }
}

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {

            -State Listen `

        '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
        '-o', 'UpdateHostKeys=no'
        '-o', 'ExitOnForwardFailure=yes'
        '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
        '-o', 'ConnectionAttempts=1'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveInterval=15'

        -FilePath $K3Tunnel.SshExe `

        }
    }

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

function Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $CimProcess
    )

    if (-not [string]::Equals(
        [string]$CimProcess.ExecutablePath,
        [string]$K3Tunnel.SshExe,
        [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )) {
        return $false
    }

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {
        return $false
    }

    $requiredText = @(
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
        ) -lt 0) {
            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {
    $processes = @(
        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
            -Filter "Name='ssh.exe'" `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    foreach ($process in $processes) {
        if (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $process) {
            $process
        }
    }
}

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {
        $existingState = Test-K3Tunnel

        if (
            $existingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
            $existingState.Healthy
        ) {
            $existingState |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $true -PassThru

            return
        }

        $existingState | Format-List | Out-Host

        throw 'A matching SSH process already exists but is not healthy or is ambiguous. It was not replaced automatically.'
    }

    $occupiedPort = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    if ($occupiedPort.Count -gt 0) {
        $occupiedPort |
            Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess |
            Format-Table -AutoSize |
            Out-Host

        throw "Local port $($K3Tunnel.LocalPort) is already occupied. No process was stopped."
    }

    foreach ($requiredFile in @(
        $K3Tunnel.SshExe
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
    )) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $requiredFile -PathType Leaf)) {
            throw "Required file does not exist: $requiredFile"
        }
    }

    $sshArguments = @(
        '-F', 'NUL'
        '-4'
        '-N'
        '-T'
        '-i', $K3Tunnel.Key
        '-o', 'IdentitiesOnly=yes'
        '-o', 'IdentityAgent=none'
        '-o', 'AddKeysToAgent=no'
        '-o', 'PreferredAuthentications=publickey'
        '-o', 'PasswordAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'BatchMode=yes'
        '-o', "UserKnownHostsFile=$($K3Tunnel.KnownHosts)"
        '-o', 'GlobalKnownHostsFile=NUL'
        '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
        '-o', 'UpdateHostKeys=no'
        '-o', 'ExitOnForwardFailure=yes'
        '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
        '-o', 'ConnectionAttempts=1'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveInterval=15'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveCountMax=3'
        '-o', 'LogLevel=ERROR'
        '-L', $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    $process = Start-Process `
        -FilePath $K3Tunnel.SshExe `
        -ArgumentList $sshArguments `
        -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -PassThru

    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(20)

    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
        $process.Refresh()

        if ($process.HasExited) {
            throw "ssh.exe exited during startup with exit code $($process.ExitCode). Run the foreground -vvv command for diagnostics."
        }

        if (Test-K3Tunnel -Quiet) {
            $state = Test-K3Tunnel

            $state |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $false -PassThru

            return
        }

        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    }

    $process.Refresh()

    if (-not $process.HasExited) {
        Stop-Process -InputObject $process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

        try {
            Wait-Process -InputObject $process -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        catch {
            # Stop-Process on Windows is forceful; this catch only preserves
            # the original startup-failure diagnosis.
        }
    }

    throw 'The new SSH process did not pass the end-to-end HTTP probe within 20 seconds and was stopped.'
}

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {
        return $false
    }

    $requiredText = @(
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
        ) -lt 0) {
            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {
    $processes = @(
        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
            -Filter "Name='ssh.exe'" `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    foreach ($process in $processes) {
        if (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $process) {
            $process
        }
    }
}

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {
        $existingState = Test-K3Tunnel

        if (
            $existingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
            $existingState.Healthy
        ) {
            $existingState |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $true -PassThru

            return
        }

        $existingState | Format-List | Out-Host

        throw 'A matching SSH process already exists but is not healthy or is ambiguous. It was not replaced automatically.'
    }

    $occupiedPort = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    if ($occupiedPort.Count -gt 0) {
        $occupiedPort |
            Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess |
            Format-Table -AutoSize |
            Out-Host

        throw "Local port $($K3Tunnel.LocalPort) is already occupied. No process was stopped."
    }

    foreach ($requiredFile in @(
        $K3Tunnel.SshExe
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
    )) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $requiredFile -PathType Leaf)) {
            throw "Required file does not exist: $requiredFile"
        }
    }

    $sshArguments = @(
        '-F', 'NUL'
        '-4'
        '-N'
        '-T'
        '-i', $K3Tunnel.Key
        '-o', 'IdentitiesOnly=yes'
        '-o', 'IdentityAgent=none'
        '-o', 'AddKeysToAgent=no'
        '-o', 'PreferredAuthentications=publickey'
        '-o', 'PasswordAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'BatchMode=yes'
        '-o', "UserKnownHostsFile=$($K3Tunnel.KnownHosts)"
        '-o', 'GlobalKnownHostsFile=NUL'
        '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
        '-o', 'UpdateHostKeys=no'
        '-o', 'ExitOnForwardFailure=yes'
        '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
        '-o', 'ConnectionAttempts=1'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveInterval=15'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveCountMax=3'
        '-o', 'LogLevel=ERROR'
        '-L', $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    $process = Start-Process `
        -FilePath $K3Tunnel.SshExe `
        -ArgumentList $sshArguments `
        -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -PassThru

    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(20)

    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
        $process.Refresh()

        if ($process.HasExited) {
            throw "ssh.exe exited during startup with exit code $($process.ExitCode). Run the foreground -vvv command for diagnostics."
        }

        if (Test-K3Tunnel -Quiet) {
            $state = Test-K3Tunnel

            $state |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $false -PassThru

            return
        }

        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    }

    $process.Refresh()

    if (-not $process.HasExited) {
        Stop-Process -InputObject $process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

        try {
            Wait-Process -InputObject $process -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        catch {
            # Stop-Process on Windows is forceful; this catch only preserves
            # the original startup-failure diagnosis.
        }
    }

    throw 'The new SSH process did not pass the end-to-end HTTP probe within 20 seconds and was stopped.'
}

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

    contentType: 'application/vnd.github.raw+json; charset=utf-8',
    text: '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> **File Browser is archived on 2026-09-01**. The last planned release has already shipped. There will be no further releases, bug fixes, or security fixes.   \n' +
      '\n' +
      '<p align="center">\n' +
      '  <img src="./branding/banner.png" width="550"/>\n' +
      '</p>\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser provides a file managing interface within a specified directory and it can be used to upload, delete, preview and edit your files. It is a **create-your-own-cloud**-kind of software where you can just install it on your server, direct it to a path and access your files through a nice web interface.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '**Background:** [Goodbye File Browser, for Real This Time](https://hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/), July 2026.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Security\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Published advisories are listed under [security advisories](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories),\n' +
      'and reporting instructions are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Two known issue classes\n' +
      'remain unaddressed and will not be fixed:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Command execution, runner, and hooks.** This feature is plagued with vulnerabilities across many published advisories, and would need a full rewrite to be made safe. It is disabled by default; if you re-enable it with `--disable-exec=false`, treat the ability to run commands as equivalent to shell access on the host. Background: [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '- **Session and JWT handling.** Sessions are self-contained JWTs rather than server-side identifiers, so they cannot be revoked, which means that logout, password changes, and renewal leave previously issued tokens valid until they expire, and the same refresh token can be redeemed repeatedly. Assume a leaked token is valid until expiry. Background: [#5216](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5216).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If you keep running File Browser, treat it as unmaintained software:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Do not expose it directly to the internet.** Put it behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and performs its own authentication.\n' +
      '- **Keep the command runner disabled.** It is off by default, so leave it off. See [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199) and [`docs/command-execution.md`](docs/command-execution.md).\n' +
      '- **Run it unprivileged, inside a container**, with only the directory you intend to serve mounted into it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Documentation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Documentation on how to install, configure, and build this project lives in [`docs`](docs) in this repository.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) documents how to build and develop the project, which remains useful to anyone forking it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## License\n' +
      '\n' +

    text: '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> **File Browser is archived on 2026-09-01**. The last planned release has already shipped. There will be no further releases, bug fixes, or security fixes.   \n' +
      '\n' +
      '<p align="center">\n' +
      '  <img src="./branding/banner.png" width="550"/>\n' +
      '</p>\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser provides a file managing interface within a specified directory and it can be used to upload, delete, preview and edit your files. It is a **create-your-own-cloud**-kind of software where you can just install it on your server, direct it to a path and access your files through a nice web interface.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '**Background:** [Goodbye File Browser, for Real This Time](https://hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/), July 2026.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Security\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Published advisories are listed under [security advisories](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories),\n' +
      'and reporting instructions are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Two known issue classes\n' +
      'remain unaddressed and will not be fixed:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Command execution, runner, and hooks.** This feature is plagued with vulnerabilities across many published advisories, and would need a full rewrite to be made safe. It is disabled by default; if you re-enable it with `--disable-exec=false`, treat the ability to run commands as equivalent to shell access on the host. Background: [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '- **Session and JWT handling.** Sessions are self-contained JWTs rather than server-side identifiers, so they cannot be revoked, which means that logout, password changes, and renewal leave previously issued tokens valid until they expire, and the same refresh token can be redeemed repeatedly. Assume a leaked token is valid until expiry. Background: [#5216](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5216).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If you keep running File Browser, treat it as unmaintained software:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Do not expose it directly to the internet.** Put it behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and performs its own authentication.\n' +
      '- **Keep the command runner disabled.** It is off by default, so leave it off. See [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199) and [`docs/command-execution.md`](docs/command-execution.md).\n' +
      '- **Run it unprivileged, inside a container**, with only the directory you intend to serve mounted into it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Documentation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Documentation on how to install, configure, and build this project lives in [`docs`](docs) in this repository.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) documents how to build and develop the project, which remains useful to anyone forking it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## License\n' +

    status: 200,
    finalUrl: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/master/docs/installation.md',
    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Installation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is a single binary and can be used as standalone executable. However, it is also available as a [Docker](https://www.docker.com) image. The installation and first time setup is quite straightforward independently of which system you use.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Binary\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The quickest and easiest way to install File Browser is to use a package manager, or our download script, which automatically fetches the latest version of File Browser for your platform. Alternatively, you can manually download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Brew\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'brew tap filebrowser/tap\n' +
      'brew install filebrowser\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Unix\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Windows\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.ps1 | iex\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Docker\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is available as two different Docker images, which can be found on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/filebrowser/filebrowser): a [bare Alpine image](#bare-alpine-image) and an [S6 Overlay image](#s6-overlay-image).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Bare Alpine Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_data:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where `filebrowser_data`, `filebrowser_database` and `filebrowser_config` are Docker [volumes](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/), where the data, database and configuration will be stored, respectively. The default configuration and database will be automatically initialized.\n' +
      '\n' +
      "The default user that runs File Browser inside the container has UID 1000 and GID 1000. If, for one reason or another, you want to run the Docker container with a different user, please consult Docker's [user documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#user).\n" +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> When using [bind mounts](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/bind-mounts/), that is, when you mount a path on the host in the container, you must manually ensure that they have the correct **permissions**. Docker does not do this automatically for you. The host directories must be readable and writable by the user running inside the container. You can use the [`chown`](https://linux.die.net/man/1/chown) command to change the owner of those paths.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### S6 Overlay Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The `s6` image is based on LinuxServer and leverages the [s6-overlay](https://github.com/just-containers/s6-overlay) system for a standard, highly customizable image. It should be used as follows:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```shell\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/srv:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -e PUID=$(id -u) \\\n' +
      '    -e PGID=$(id -g) \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser:s6\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- `/path/to/srv` contains the files root directory for File Browser\n' +
      '- `/path/to/config` contains a `settings.json` file\n' +
      '- `/path/to/database` contains a `filebrowser.db` file\n' +
      '\n' +
      "Both `settings.json` and `filebrowser.db` will automatically be initialized if they don't exist.\n" +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## First Boot\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Your instance is now up and running. File Browser will automatically bootstrap a database, in which the configuration and the users are stored. You can find the address in which your instance is running, as well as the randomly generated password for the user `admin`, in the console logs.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> The automatically generated password for the user `admin` is only displayed once. If you fail to remember it, you will need to manually delete the database and start File Browser again.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Although this is the fastest way to bootstrap an instance, we recommend you to take a look at other possible options, by checking [`config init`](cli/filebrowser-config-init.md) and [`config set`](cli/filebrowser-config-set.md), to make the installation as safe and customized as it can be.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If your goal is to have a public-facing deployment, we recommend taking a look at the [deployment](deployment.md) page for more information on how you can secure your installation.\n'

    text: '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> **File Browser is archived on 2026-09-01**. The last planned release has already shipped. There will be no further releases, bug fixes, or security fixes.   \n' +
      '\n' +
      '<p align="center">\n' +
      '  <img src="./branding/banner.png" width="550"/>\n' +
      '</p>\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser provides a file managing interface within a specified directory and it can be used to upload, delete, preview and edit your files. It is a **create-your-own-cloud**-kind of software where you can just install it on your server, direct it to a path and access your files through a nice web interface.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '**Background:** [Goodbye File Browser, for Real This Time](https://hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/), July 2026.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Security\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Published advisories are listed under [security advisories](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories),\n' +
      'and reporting instructions are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Two known issue classes\n' +
      'remain unaddressed and will not be fixed:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Command execution, runner, and hooks.** This feature is plagued with vulnerabilities across many published advisories, and would need a full rewrite to be made safe. It is disabled by default; if you re-enable it with `--disable-exec=false`, treat the ability to run commands as equivalent to shell access on the host. Background: [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '- **Session and JWT handling.** Sessions are self-contained JWTs rather than server-side identifiers, so they cannot be revoked, which means that logout, password changes, and renewal leave previously issued tokens valid until they expire, and the same refresh token can be redeemed repeatedly. Assume a leaked token is valid until expiry. Background: [#5216](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5216).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If you keep running File Browser, treat it as unmaintained software:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Do not expose it directly to the internet.** Put it behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and performs its own authentication.\n' +
      '- **Keep the command runner disabled.** It is off by default, so leave it off. See [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199) and [`docs/command-execution.md`](docs/command-execution.md).\n' +
      '- **Run it unprivileged, inside a container**, with only the directory you intend to serve mounted into it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Documentation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Documentation on how to install, configure, and build this project lives in [`docs`](docs) in this repository.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) documents how to build and develop the project, which remains useful to anyone forking it.\n' +
      '\n' +

    text: '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> **File Browser is archived on 2026-09-01**. The last planned release has already shipped. There will be no further releases, bug fixes, or security fixes.   \n' +
      '\n' +
      '<p align="center">\n' +
      '  <img src="./branding/banner.png" width="550"/>\n' +
      '</p>\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser provides a file managing interface within a specified directory and it can be used to upload, delete, preview and edit your files. It is a **create-your-own-cloud**-kind of software where you can just install it on your server, direct it to a path and access your files through a nice web interface.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '**Background:** [Goodbye File Browser, for Real This Time](https://hacdias.com/2026/07/28/filebrowser/), July 2026.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Security\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Published advisories are listed under [security advisories](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories),\n' +
      'and reporting instructions are in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). Two known issue classes\n' +
      'remain unaddressed and will not be fixed:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Command execution, runner, and hooks.** This feature is plagued with vulnerabilities across many published advisories, and would need a full rewrite to be made safe. It is disabled by default; if you re-enable it with `--disable-exec=false`, treat the ability to run commands as equivalent to shell access on the host. Background: [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '- **Session and JWT handling.** Sessions are self-contained JWTs rather than server-side identifiers, so they cannot be revoked, which means that logout, password changes, and renewal leave previously issued tokens valid until they expire, and the same refresh token can be redeemed repeatedly. Assume a leaked token is valid until expiry. Background: [#5216](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5216).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If you keep running File Browser, treat it as unmaintained software:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- **Do not expose it directly to the internet.** Put it behind a reverse proxy that terminates TLS and performs its own authentication.\n' +
      '- **Keep the command runner disabled.** It is off by default, so leave it off. See [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199) and [`docs/command-execution.md`](docs/command-execution.md).\n' +
      '- **Run it unprivileged, inside a container**, with only the directory you intend to serve mounted into it.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Documentation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Documentation on how to install, configure, and build this project lives in [`docs`](docs) in this repository.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) documents how to build and develop the project, which remains useful to anyone forking it.\n' +
      '\n' +

    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Installation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is a single binary and can be used as standalone executable. However, it is also available as a [Docker](https://www.docker.com) image. The installation and first time setup is quite straightforward independently of which system you use.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Binary\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The quickest and easiest way to install File Browser is to use a package manager, or our download script, which automatically fetches the latest version of File Browser for your platform. Alternatively, you can manually download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Brew\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'brew tap filebrowser/tap\n' +
      'brew install filebrowser\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Unix\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Windows\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.ps1 | iex\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Docker\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is available as two different Docker images, which can be found on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/filebrowser/filebrowser): a [bare Alpine image](#bare-alpine-image) and an [S6 Overlay image](#s6-overlay-image).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Bare Alpine Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_data:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where `filebrowser_data`, `filebrowser_database` and `filebrowser_config` are Docker [volumes](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/), where the data, database and configuration will be stored, respectively. The default configuration and database will be automatically initialized.\n' +
      '\n' +
      "The default user that runs File Browser inside the container has UID 1000 and GID 1000.       '\n' +
      '## Supported Versions\n' +
      '\n' +
      'No version receives security fixes. The last planned release has already shipped and no further changes will be merged.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '| Version | Supported |\n' +

      '\n' +
      '## Before Reporting\n' +
      '\n' +
      'This project is being wound down. To avoid duplicates, first check the [existing advisories](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories) and open issues, and confirm:\n' +
      '\n' +

      '\n' +
      '## Reporting a Vulnerability\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Until 2026-09-01, report privately via the [Security](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security) page. After that date this repository is read-only and reports can no longer be submitted.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Please include, where possible:\n' +
      '\n' +

      '- Steps to reproduce\n' +
      '- Recommended remediation, if any\n' +

    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Installation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is a single binary and can be used as standalone executable. However, it is also available as a [Docker](https://www.docker.com) image. The installation and first time setup is quite straightforward independently of which system you use.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Binary\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The quickest and easiest way to install File Browser is to use a package manager, or our download script, which automatically fetches the latest version of File Browser for your platform. Alternatively, you can manually download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Brew\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'brew tap filebrowser/tap\n' +
      'brew install filebrowser\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Unix\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Windows\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.ps1 | iex\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Docker\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is available as two different Docker images, which can be found on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/filebrowser/filebrowser): a [bare Alpine image](#bare-alpine-image) and an [S6 Overlay image](#s6-overlay-image).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Bare Alpine Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_data:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where `filebrowser_data`, `filebrowser_database` and `filebrowser_config` are Docker [volumes](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/), where the data, database and configuration will be stored, respectively. The default configuration and database will be automatically initialized.\n' +
      '\n' +
      "The default user that runs File Browser inside the container has UID 1000 and GID 1000. If, for one reason or another, you want to run the Docker container with a different user, please consult Docker's [user documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#user).\n" +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> When using [bind mounts](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/bind-mounts/), that is, when you mount a path on the host in the container, you must manually ensure that they have the correct **permissions**. Docker does not do this automatically for you. The host directories must be readable and writable by the user running inside the container. You can use the [`chown`](https://linux.die.net/man/1/chown) command to change the owner of those paths.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### S6 Overlay Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The `s6` image is based on LinuxServer and leverages the [s6-overlay](https://github.com/just-containers/s6-overlay) system for a standard, highly customizable image. It should be used as follows:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```shell\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/srv:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -e PUID=$(id -u) \\\n' +
      '    -e PGID=$(id -g) \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser:s6\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- `/path/to/srv` contains the files root directory for File Browser\n' +
      '- `/path/to/config` contains a `settings.json` file\n' +
      '- `/path/to/database` contains a `filebrowser.db` file\n' +
      '\n' +
      "Both `settings.json` and `filebrowser.db` will automatically be initialized if they don't exist.\n" +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## First Boot\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Your instance is now up and running. File Browser will automatically bootstrap a database, in which the configuration and the users are stored. You can find the address in which your instance is running, as well as the randomly generated password for the user `admin`, in the console logs.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> The automatically generated password for the user `admin` is only displayed once. If you fail to remember it, you will need to manually delete the database and start File Browser again.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Although this is the fastest way to bootstrap an instance, we recommend you to take a look at other possible options, by checking [`config init`](cli/filebrowser-config-init.md) and [`config set`](cli/filebrowser-config-set.md), to make the installation as safe and customized as it can be.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If your goal is to have a public-facing deployment, we recommend taking a look at the [deployment](deployment.md) page for more information on how you can secure your installation.\n'

    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Command Execution\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!CAUTION]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> The **hook runner** and **interactive shell** functionalities have been disabled for all existent and new installations by default from version v2.33.8 and onwards, due to continuous and known security vulnerabilities. You should only use this feature if you are aware of all of the security risks involved. For more up to date information, consult issue [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Hook Runner\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The hook runner is a feature that enables you to execute any shell command you want before or after a certain event. Right now, these are the events:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '* Copy\n' +
      '* Rename\n' +
      '* Upload\n' +
      '* Delete\n' +
      '* Save\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Also, during the execution of the commands set for those hooks, there will be some environment variables available to help you perform your commands:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '* `FILE` with the full absolute path to the changed file.\n' +
      "* `SCOPE` with the path to user's scope.\n" +
      '* `TRIGGER` with the name of the event.\n' +
      "* `USERNAME` with the user's username.\n" +
      '* `DESTINATION` with the absolute path to the destination. Only used for **copy** and **rename.**\n' +
      '\n' +
      'At this moment, you can edit the commands via the command line interface, using the following commands \\(please check the flag `--help` to know more about them\\):\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```bash\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds add before_copy "echo $FILE"\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds rm before_copy 0\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds ls\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Or you can use the web interface to manage them via **Settings** â†?**Global Settings**.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Interactive Shell\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Within File Browser you can toggle the shell (`< >` icon at the top right) and this will open a shell command window at the bottom of the screen. This functionality can be turned on using the environment variable `FB_DISABLE_EXEC=false` or the flag `--disable-exec=false`.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'By default no commands are available as the command list is empty. To enable commands these need to either be done on a per-user basis (including for the Admin user).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'You can do this by adding them in Settings > User Management > (edit user) > Commands or to *apply to all new users created from that point forward* they can be set in Settings > Global Settings\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> If using a proxy manager then remember to enable websockets support for the File Browser proxy\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> If using Docker and you want to add a new command that is not in the base image then you will need to build a custom Docker image using `filebrowser/filebrowser` as a base image.  For example to add 7z:\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> ```docker\n' +
      '> FROM filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '> RUN sudo apt install p7zip-full\n' +
      '> ```\n'

    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Installation\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is a single binary and can be used as standalone executable. However, it is also available as a [Docker](https://www.docker.com) image. The installation and first time setup is quite straightforward independently of which system you use.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Binary\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The quickest and easiest way to install File Browser is to use a package manager, or our download script, which automatically fetches the latest version of File Browser for your platform. Alternatively, you can manually download the binary from the [releases page](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Brew\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'brew tap filebrowser/tap\n' +
      'brew install filebrowser\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Unix\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Windows\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.ps1 | iex\n' +
      'filebrowser -r /path/to/your/files\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Docker\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is available as two different Docker images, which can be found on [Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/r/filebrowser/filebrowser): a [bare Alpine image](#bare-alpine-image) and an [S6 Overlay image](#s6-overlay-image).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Bare Alpine Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```sh\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_data:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v filebrowser_config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where `filebrowser_data`, `filebrowser_database` and `filebrowser_config` are Docker [volumes](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/volumes/), where the data, database and configuration will be stored, respectively. The default configuration and database will be automatically initialized.\n' +
      '\n' +
      "The default user that runs File Browser inside the container has UID 1000 and GID 1000. If, for one reason or another, you want to run the Docker container with a different user, please consult Docker's [user documentation](https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/run/#user).\n" +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> When using [bind mounts](https://docs.docker.com/engine/storage/bind-mounts/), that is, when you mount a path on the host in the container, you must manually ensure that they have the correct **permissions**. Docker does not do this automatically for you. The host directories must be readable and writable by the user running inside the container. You can use the [`chown`](https://linux.die.net/man/1/chown) command to change the owner of those paths.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### S6 Overlay Image\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The `s6` image is based on LinuxServer and leverages the [s6-overlay](https://github.com/just-containers/s6-overlay) system for a standard, highly customizable image. It should be used as follows:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```shell\n' +
      'docker run \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/srv:/srv \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/database:/database \\\n' +
      '    -v /path/to/config:/config \\\n' +
      '    -e PUID=$(id -u) \\\n' +
      '    -e PGID=$(id -g) \\\n' +
      '    -p 8080:80 \\\n' +
      '    filebrowser/filebrowser:s6\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Where:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '- `/path/to/srv` contains the files root directory for File Browser\n' +
      '- `/path/to/config` contains a `settings.json` file\n' +
      '- `/path/to/database` contains a `filebrowser.db` file\n' +
      '\n' +
      "Both `settings.json` and `filebrowser.db` will automatically be initialized if they don't exist.\n" +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser is now up and running. Read the ["First Boot"](#first-boot) section for more information.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## First Boot\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Your instance is now up and running. File Browser will automatically bootstrap a database, in which the configuration and the users are stored. You can find the address in which your instance is running, as well as the randomly generated password for the user `admin`, in the console logs.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> The automatically generated password for the user `admin` is only displayed once. If you fail to remember it, you will need to manually delete the database and start File Browser again.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Although this is the fastest way to bootstrap an instance, we recommend you to take a look at other possible options, by checking [`config init`](cli/filebrowser-config-init.md) and [`config set`](cli/filebrowser-config-set.md), to make the installation as safe and customized as it can be.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'If your goal is to have a public-facing deployment, we recommend taking a look at the [deployment](deployment.md) page for more information on how you can secure your installation.\n'

    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '# Command Execution\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!CAUTION]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> The **hook runner** and **interactive shell** functionalities have been disabled for all existent and new installations by default from version v2.33.8 and onwards, due to continuous and known security vulnerabilities. You should only use this feature if you are aware of all of the security risks involved. For more up to date information, consult issue [#5199](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues/5199).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Hook Runner\n' +
      '\n' +
      'The hook runner is a feature that enables you to execute any shell command you want before or after a certain event. Right now, these are the events:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '* Copy\n' +
      '* Rename\n' +
      '* Upload\n' +
      '* Delete\n' +
      '* Save\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Also, during the execution of the commands set for those hooks, there will be some environment variables available to help you perform your commands:\n' +
      '\n' +
      '* `FILE` with the full absolute path to the changed file.\n' +
      "* `SCOPE` with the path to user's scope.\n" +
      '* `TRIGGER` with the name of the event.\n' +
      "* `USERNAME` with the user's username.\n" +
      '* `DESTINATION` with the absolute path to the destination. Only used for **copy** and **rename.**\n' +
      '\n' +
      'At this moment, you can edit the commands via the command line interface, using the following commands \\(please check the flag `--help` to know more about them\\):\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```bash\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds add before_copy "echo $FILE"\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds rm before_copy 0\n' +
      'filebrowser cmds ls\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Or you can use the web interface to manage them via **Settings** â†?**Global Settings**.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Interactive Shell\n' +
      '\n' +
      'Within File Browser you can toggle the shell (`< >` icon at the top right) and this will open a shell command window at the bottom of the screen. This functionality can be turned on using the environment variable `FB_DISABLE_EXEC=false` or the flag `--disable-exec=false`.\n' +
      '\n' +
      'By default no commands are available as the command list is empty. To enable commands these need to either be done on a per-user basis (including for the Admin user).\n' +
      '\n' +
      'You can do this by adding them in Settings > User Management > (edit user) > Commands or to *apply to all new users created from that point forward* they can be set in Settings > Global Settings\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> If using a proxy manager then remember to enable websockets support for the File Browser proxy\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!NOTE]\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> If using Docker and you want to add a new command that is not in the base image then you will need to build a custom Docker image using `filebrowser/filebrowser` as a base image.  For example to add 7z:\n' +
      '> \n' +
      '> ```docker\n' +
      '> FROM filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '> RUN sudo apt install p7zip-full\n' +
      '> ```\n'

running the latest [FileBrowser version](https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/releases) or have an issue updating.\\n\\n### Version\\n\\n```Text\\nAll\\n```\\n\\n### Description\\n\\n@mtausig\'s report:\\n\\n> The usage of the session token can be improved:\\n>\\n> - JWT are not suitable to be used as a session token and should be replaced by a random identifier stored by the application\\n> - Storage and transmission of the tokens are also strange. They are stored in the browser\'s cookie jar and in the local storage and furthermore transmitted multiple times with many requests (Once as a Cookie, once via the X-Auth header). While this is not directly vulnerable, it introduces unnecessary complexity that can easily lead to errors in the future\\n> - The same Refresh Token can be renewed at /api/renew multiple times. This should only work a single time per token.\\n\\nAnd the following:\\n\\n- https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-7xwp-2cpp-p8r7\\n- https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/security/advisories/GHSA-v7vv-5wj2-gfcj\\n\\n### Tasks\\n\\n- [ ] Replace JWT session token by a random identifier stored in the database\\n- [ ] Replace Refresh Token by non-JWT random identifier stored in the database\\n- [ ] Front-end fetches user information via another means that is not the JWT\\n- [ ] Upon logout, invalidate identifier\\n- [ ]     text: '## Self-Registration (Signup)\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser allows you to enable user self-registration (signup). This can be enabled via **Settings â†?Global Settings**, or with `filebrowser config set --signup`. Self-registered users inherit the configured **user defaults**, including the scope.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      "> By default, the user scope is the server's root, so a self-registered user could read,\n" +
      '> modify, and delete every file File Browser serves. To prevent this, either:\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> a. Enable `createUserDir` so each user gets their own directory; or\n' +
      '> b. If users are meant to share files, set the default scope to something other than the root.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Fail2ban\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser does not natively support protection against brute force attacks. Therefore, we suggest using something like [fail2ban](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban), which takes care of that by tracking the logs of your File Browser instance. For more information on how fail2ban works, please refer to their [wiki](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/wiki).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Filter Configuration\n' +
      '\n' +
      "An example filter configuration targeted at matching File Browser's logs.\n" +
      '\n' +
      '```ini\n' +
      '[INCLUDES]\n' +
      'before = common.conf\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[Definition]\n' +
      'datepattern = `^%%Y\\/%%m\\/%%d %%H:%%M:%%S`\n' +
      'failregex   = `\\/api\\/login: 403 <HOST> *`\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Jail Configuration\n' +
      '\n' +
      'An example jail configuration. You should fill it with the path of the logs of File Browser, as well as the port where it is running at.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```ini\n' +
      '[filebrowser]\n' +
      '\n' +
      'enabled = true\n' +
      'port = [your_port]\n' +
      'filter = filebrowser\n' +
      'logpath = [your_log_path]\n' +
      'maxretry = 10\n' +
      'bantime = 10m\n' +
      'findtime = 10m\n' +
      'banaction = iptables-allports\n' +
      'banaction_allports = iptables-allports\n' +
      '```\n'

      `<a class=u-photo href=https://hacdias.com/avatar/512.jpg>(Photo)</a></div></header><div class=e-content><p>Yesterday, I published the last planned release of <a href=https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser rel='noopener noreferrer'>File Browser</a>. It includes a few security fixes and a notice about the wind-down of the project. Alongside it, I announced that this was the last planned release and updated the repository so that it’s ready to be archived on September 1st. For many people this came as a surprise. For those who’ve been following the project from close by, probably not. Either way, I wanted to write a bit about the decision and how we got to this point.</p><figure><picture><source srcset="https://media.hacdias.com/image/600/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 600w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/900/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 900w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 1800w" type=image/webp><source srcset="https://media.hacdias.com/image/600/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 600w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/900/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 900w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 1800w" type=image/jpeg><img src=https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg alt="Screenshot of File Browser" width=3541 height=2160 loading=lazy></picture><figcaption>Screenshot of File Browser</figcaption></figure><h2 id=how-we-got-here>How We Got Here</h2><p>This isn’t the first time I’ve said goodbye. In 2020, I wrote <a href=/2020/01/23/bye-filebrowser/><em>Goodbye File Browser</em></a> and handed the project over to someone in the community. Maintainers came and went. At the end of last year, I noticed the project hadn’t been maintained for a year or so, and I took the reins again. It felt better to do and say something than to keep issues and PRs unanswered.</p><p>In March, I wrote <a href=/2026/03/11/filebrowser/><em>Update on File Browser</em></a>: how the project came to be, why it is the way it is, and why I had put it in maintenance-only mode. I won’t repeat all of that here, and I’d recommend reading it if you’re interested. The TLDR is that I started this project as a 15 year old, more than ten years ago, because I wanted a single-binary browser based File Browser. It became far more popular than I could ever have envisioned – over 35 000 stars on GitHub – and it never stopped being code written by a 15 year old.</p><h2 id=why-im-stopping>Why Iâ€™m Stopping</h2><p>Not much has changed since March. The security vulnerability advisories kept coming. I reviewed each one and write a fix – sometimes myself, sometimes with Claude, sometimes a better fix than others. For certain features, I decided not to touch them at all, because fixing the real source of the problem would require rewriting the whole feature. Those are documented in the repository, and they will stay unfixed.</p><p>What I’ve come to accept is that this can’t be patched into shape. File Browser would need to be rewritten from the ground up, with security and a good API in mind, neither of which was on my mind when I was 15. Sessions are the clearest example: expired tokens keep working in some situations, and logging out doesn’t invalidate a token, so if someone stole it, it still works. There are many things like this, and each one is a rewrite of its own.</p><p>Doing any of it well also takes time. I’ve been spending a few hours most weekends going through issues and advisories, and it’s just not enough. I can tell the quality isn’t what I’d want it to be. To make something better, I’d need much more time than I have.</p><p>Mostly, though, the will isn’t there anymore. For me this is a project from over ten years ago. It reached its goal, it happened to become popular, and maintaining a codebase I don’t think is good doesn’t give me any pleasure. Another year of weekends wouldn’t change that. People have told me over the past years that I should stop, and they’ve been right all along. They see the frustration in me.</p><h2 id=what-now>What Now</h2><p>The project is prepared to be archived. No more issues or pull requests can be opened until the archival date. You can still report security vulnerabilities, which will be made public on the day of archival, or before. However, they will not be addressed.</p><p>The project is delivered as-is. If you want to keep using it, treat it as any other piece of deprecated software: use at your own risk, don’t expose it to the public Internet, and be mindful of the known security vulnerabilities listed on the README and on the advisories page.</p><p>I’d rather have you, or any user, using a different alternative. I can’t recommend any specific alternative, as I haven’t compared them side-by-side, or even used them. What I can point you to is <a href=https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/s/8LcLmL1rJ4 rel='noopener noreferrer'>this post on r/selfhosted</a>, where people have been sharing the projects they’ve been using for quite some time, or check <a href=https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted rel='noopener noreferrer'>Awesome Self-hosted</a>. That’s where I’d start.</p><hr><p>Thanks to everyone that has ever contributed to the project, and for all the effort that has ever been put here. It’s been quite a long journey for something that was never meant to be anything else other than a personal side project.</p><p>Goodbye File Browser, for real this time! ðŸ‘‹</p></div><footer><ul class='tb small'><li><strong>ðŸ“ Where</strong>\n` +

    text: '## Self-Registration (Signup)\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser allows you to enable user self-registration (signup). This can be enabled via **Settings â†?Global Settings**, or with `filebrowser config set --signup`. Self-registered users inherit the configured **user defaults**, including the scope.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '> [!WARNING]\n' +
      '>\n' +
      "> By default, the user scope is the server's root, so a self-registered user could read,\n" +
      '> modify, and delete every file File Browser serves. To prevent this, either:\n' +
      '>\n' +
      '> a. Enable `createUserDir` so each user gets their own directory; or\n' +
      '> b. If users are meant to share files, set the default scope to something other than the root.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '## Fail2ban\n' +
      '\n' +
      'File Browser does not natively support protection against brute force attacks. Therefore, we suggest using something like [fail2ban](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban), which takes care of that by tracking the logs of your File Browser instance. For more information on how fail2ban works, please refer to their [wiki](https://github.com/fail2ban/fail2ban/wiki).\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Filter Configuration\n' +
      '\n' +
      "An example filter configuration targeted at matching File Browser's logs.\n" +
      '\n' +
      '```ini\n' +
      '[INCLUDES]\n' +
      'before = common.conf\n' +
      '\n' +
      '[Definition]\n' +
      'datepattern = `^%%Y\\/%%m\\/%%d %%H:%%M:%%S`\n' +
      'failregex   = `\\/api\\/login: 403 <HOST> *`\n' +
      '```\n' +
      '\n' +
      '### Jail Configuration\n' +
      '\n' +
      'An example jail configuration. You should fill it with the path of the logs of File Browser, as well as the port where it is running at.\n' +
      '\n' +
      '```ini\n' +
      '[filebrowser]\n' +
      '\n' +
      'enabled = true\n' +
      'port = [your_port]\n' +
      'filter = filebrowser\n' +
      'logpath = [your_log_path]\n' +
      'maxretry = 10\n' +
      'bantime = 10m\n' +
      'findtime = 10m\n' +
      'banaction = iptables-allports\n' +
      'banaction_allports = iptables-allports\n' +
      '```\n'
