      `<a class=u-photo href=https://hacdias.com/avatar/512.jpg>(Photo)</a></div></header><div class=e-content><p>Yesterday, I published the last planned release of <a href=https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser rel='noopener noreferrer'>File Browser</a>. It includes a few security fixes and a notice about the wind-down of the project. Alongside it, I announced that this was the last planned release and updated the repository so that it’s ready to be archived on September 1st. For many people this came as a surprise. For those who’ve been following the project from close by, probably not. Either way, I wanted to write a bit about the decision and how we got to this point.</p><figure><picture><source srcset="https://media.hacdias.com/image/600/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 600w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/900/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 900w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.webp 1800w" type=image/webp><source srcset="https://media.hacdias.com/image/600/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 600w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/900/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 900w, https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg 1800w" type=image/jpeg><img src=https://media.hacdias.com/image/1800/2026-03-11-filebrowser.jpeg alt="Screenshot of File Browser" width=3541 height=2160 loading=lazy></picture><figcaption>Screenshot of File Browser</figcaption></figure><h2 id=how-we-got-here>How We Got Here</h2><p>This isn’t the first time I’ve said goodbye. In 2020, I wrote <a href=/2020/01/23/bye-filebrowser/><em>Goodbye File Browser</em></a> and handed the project over to someone in the community. Maintainers came and went. At the end of last year, I noticed the project hadn’t been maintained for a year or so, and I took the reins again. It felt better to do and say something than to keep issues and PRs unanswered.</p><p>In March, I wrote <a href=/2026/03/11/filebrowser/><em>Update on File Browser</em></a>: how the project came to be, why it is the way it is, and why I had put it in maintenance-only mode. I won’t repeat all of that here, and I’d recommend reading it if you’re interested. The TLDR is that I started this project as a 15 year old, more than ten years ago, because I wanted a single-binary browser based File Browser. It became far more popular than I could ever have envisioned – over 35 000 stars on GitHub – and it never stopped being code written by a 15 year old.</p><h2 id=why-im-stopping>Why Iâ€™m Stopping</h2><p>Not much has changed since March. The security vulnerability advisories kept coming. I reviewed each one and write a fix – sometimes myself, sometimes with Claude, sometimes a better fix than others. For certain features, I decided not to touch them at all, because fixing the real source of the problem would require rewriting the whole feature. Those are documented in the repository, and they will stay unfixed.</p><p>What I’ve come to accept is that this can’t be patched into shape. File Browser would need to be rewritten from the ground up, with security and a good API in mind, neither of which was on my mind when I was 15. Sessions are the clearest example: expired tokens keep working in some situations, and logging out doesn’t invalidate a token, so if someone stole it, it still works. There are many things like this, and each one is a rewrite of its own.</p><p>Doing any of it well also takes time. I’ve been spending a few hours most weekends going through issues and advisories, and it’s just not enough. I can tell the quality isn’t what I’d want it to be. To make something better, I’d need much more time than I have.</p><p>Mostly, though, the will isn’t there anymore. For me this is a project from over ten years ago. It reached its goal, it happened to become popular, and maintaining a codebase I don’t think is good doesn’t give me any pleasure. Another year of weekends wouldn’t change that. People have told me over the past years that I should stop, and they’ve been right all along. They see the frustration in me.</p><h2 id=what-now>What Now</h2><p>The project is prepared to be archived. No more issues or pull requests can be opened until the archival date. You can still report security vulnerabilities, which will be made public on the day of archival, or before. However, they will not be addressed.</p><p>The project is delivered as-is. If you want to keep using it, treat it as any other piece of deprecated software: use at your own risk, don’t expose it to the public Internet, and be mindful of the known security vulnerabilities listed on the README and on the advisories page.</p><p>I’d rather have you, or any user, using a different alternative. I can’t recommend any specific alternative, as I haven’t compared them side-by-side, or even used them. What I can point you to is <a href=https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/s/8LcLmL1rJ4 rel='noopener noreferrer'>this post on r/selfhosted</a>, where people have been sharing the projects they’ve been using for quite some time, or check <a href=https://github.com/awesome-selfhosted/awesome-selfhosted rel='noopener noreferrer'>Awesome Self-hosted</a>. That’s where I’d start.</p><hr><p>Thanks to everyone that has ever contributed to the project, and for all the effort that has ever been put here. It’s been quite a long journey for something that was never meant to be anything else other than a personal side project.</p><p>Goodbye File Browser, for real this time! ðŸ‘‹</p></div><footer><ul class='tb small'><li><strong>ðŸ“ Where</strong>\n` +

    u: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh',
    status: 200,
    finalUrl: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh',
    contentType: 'text/plain; charset=utf-8',
    text: '#!/usr/bin/env bash\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#           File Browser Installer Script\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#   GitHub: https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser\n' +
      '#   Issues: https://github.com/filebrowser/filebrowser/issues\n' +
      '#   Requires: bash, mv, rm, tr, type, grep, sed, curl/wget, tar (or unzip on OSX and Windows)\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#   This script installs File Browser to your path.\n' +
      '#   Usage:\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#   \t$ curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      '#   \t  or\n' +
      '#   \t$ wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/filebrowser/get/master/get.sh | bash\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#   In automated environments, you may want to run as root.\n' +
      '#   If using curl, we recommend using the -fsSL flags.\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '#   This should work on Mac, Linux, and BSD systems, and\n' +
      '#   hopefully Windows with Cygwin. Please open an issue if\n' +
      '#   you notice any bugs.\n' +
      '#\n' +
      '\n' +
      'install_filemanager()\n' +
      '{\n' +
      `\ttrap 'echo -e "Aborted, error $? in command: $BASH_COMMAND"; trap ERR; return 1' ERR\n` +
      '\tfilemanager_os="unsupported"\n' +
      '\tfilemanager_arch="unknown"\n' +
      '\tinstall_path="/usr/local/bin"\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\t# Termux on Android has $PREFIX set which already ends with /usr\n' +
      '\tif [[ -n "$ANDROID_ROOT" && -n "$PREFIX" ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tinstall_path="$PREFIX/bin"\n' +
      '\tfi\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\t# Fall back to /usr/bin if necessary\n' +
      '\tif [[ ! -d $install_path ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tinstall_path="/usr/bin"\n' +
      '\tfi\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\t# Not every platform has or needs sudo (https://termux.com/linux.html)\n' +
      '\t((EUID)) && [[ -z "$ANDROID_ROOT" ]] && sudo_cmd="sudo"\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\t#########################\n' +
      '\t# Which OS and version? #\n' +
      '\t#########################\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\tfilemanager_bin="filebrowser"\n' +
      '\tfilemanager_dl_ext=".tar.gz"\n' +
      '\n' +
      '\t# NOTE: `uname -m` is more accurate and universal than `arch`\n' +
      '\t# See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uname\n' +
      '\tunamem="$(uname -m)"\n' +
      '\tcase $unamem in\n' +
      '\t*aarch64*|arm64)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="arm64";;\n' +
      '\t*riscv64*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="riscv64";;\n' +
      '\t*64*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="amd64";;\n' +
      '\t*86*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="386";;\n' +
      '\t*armv5*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="armv5";;\n' +
      '\t*armv6*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="armv6";;\n' +
      '\t*armv7*)\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_arch="armv7";;\n' +
      '\t*)\n' +
      '\t\techo "Aborted, unsupported or unknown architecture: $unamem"\n' +
      '\t\treturn 2\n' +
      '\t\t;;\n' +
      '\tesac\n' +
      '\n' +
      `\tunameu="$(tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' <<<$(uname))"\n` +
      '\tif [[ $unameu == *DARWIN* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="darwin"\n' +
      '\telif [[ $unameu == *LINUX* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="linux"\n' +
      '\telif [[ $unameu == *FREEBSD* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="freebsd"\n' +
      '\telif [[ $unameu == *NETBSD* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="netbsd"\n' +
      '\telif [[ $unameu == *OPENBSD* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="openbsd"\n' +
      '\telif [[ $unameu == *WIN* || $unameu == MSYS* ]]; then\n' +
      '\t\t# Should catch cygwin\n' +
      '\t\tsudo_cmd=""\n' +
      '\t\tfilemanager_os="windows"\n' +

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.

function Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $CimProcess
    )

    if (-not [string]::Equals(
        [string]$CimProcess.ExecutablePath,
        [string]$K3Tunnel.SshExe,
        [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )) {
        return $false
    }

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {
        return $false
    }

    $requiredText = @(
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
        ) -lt 0) {
            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {
    $processes = @(
        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
            -Filter "Name='ssh.exe'" `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    foreach ($process in $processes) {
        if (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $process) {
            $process
        }
    }
}

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {
        $existingState = Test-K3Tunnel

        if (
            $existingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
            $existingState.Healthy
        ) {
            $existingState |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $true -PassThru

            return
        }

        $existingState | Format-List | Out-Host

        throw 'A matching SSH process already exists but is not healthy or is ambiguous. It was not replaced automatically.'
    }

    $occupiedPort = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    if ($occupiedPort.Count -gt 0) {
        $occupiedPort |
            Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess |
            Format-Table -AutoSize |
            Out-Host

        throw "Local port $($K3Tunnel.LocalPort) is already occupied. No process was stopped."
    }

    foreach ($requiredFile in @(
        $K3Tunnel.SshExe
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
    )) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $requiredFile -PathType Leaf)) {
            throw "Required file does not exist: $requiredFile"
        }
    }

    $sshArguments = @(
        '-F', 'NUL'
        '-4'
        '-N'
        '-T'
        '-i', $K3Tunnel.Key
        '-o', 'IdentitiesOnly=yes'
        '-o', 'IdentityAgent=none'
        '-o', 'AddKeysToAgent=no'
        '-o', 'PreferredAuthentications=publickey'
        '-o', 'PasswordAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'BatchMode=yes'
        '-o', "UserKnownHostsFile=$($K3Tunnel.KnownHosts)"
        '-o', 'GlobalKnownHostsFile=NUL'
        '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
        '-o', 'UpdateHostKeys=no'
        '-o', 'ExitOnForwardFailure=yes'
        '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
        '-o', 'ConnectionAttempts=1'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveInterval=15'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveCountMax=3'
        '-o', 'LogLevel=ERROR'
        '-L', $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    $process = Start-Process `
        -FilePath $K3Tunnel.SshExe `
        -ArgumentList $sshArguments `
        -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -PassThru

    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(20)

    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {
        $process.Refresh()

        if ($process.HasExited) {
            throw "ssh.exe exited during startup with exit code $($process.ExitCode). Run the foreground -vvv command for diagnostics."
        }

        if (Test-K3Tunnel -Quiet) {
            $state = Test-K3Tunnel

            $state |
                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $false -PassThru

            return
        }

        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 250
    }

    $process.Refresh()

    if (-not $process.HasExited) {
        Stop-Process -InputObject $process -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

        try {
            Wait-Process -InputObject $process -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
        }
        catch {
            # Stop-Process on Windows is forceful; this catch only preserves
            # the original startup-failure diagnosis.
        }
    }

    throw 'The new SSH process did not pass the end-to-end HTTP probe within 20 seconds and was stopped.'
}

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

function Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $CimProcess
    )

    if (-not [string]::Equals(
        [string]$CimProcess.ExecutablePath,
        [string]$K3Tunnel.SshExe,
        [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
    )) {
        return $false
    }

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {
        return $false
    }

    $requiredText = @(
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination
    )

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
        ) -lt 0) {
            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {
    $processes = @(
        Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
            -Filter "Name='ssh.exe'" `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    foreach ($process in $processes) {
        if (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $process) {
            $process
        }
    }
}

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {
        $existingState = Test-K3Tunnel

        if (
            $existingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
            $existingState.Healthy

                Add-Member -NotePropertyName Reused -NotePropertyValue $true -PassThru

            return
        }

        $existingState | Format-List | Out-Host

        throw 'A matching SSH process already exists but is not healthy or is ambiguous. It was not replaced automatically.'
    }

        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    if ($occupiedPort.Count -gt 0) {

            Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess |
            Format-Table -AutoSize |
            Out-Host

        throw "Local port $($K3Tunnel.LocalPort) is already occupied. No process was stopped."
    }

    foreach ($requiredFile in @(
        $K3Tunnel.SshExe
        $K3Tunnel.Key
        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
    )) {
        if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $requiredFile -PathType Leaf)) {

        '-4'
        '-N'
        '-T'
        '-i', $K3Tunnel.Key
        '-o', 'IdentitiesOnly=yes'
        '-o', 'IdentityAgent=none'

        '-o', 'PreferredAuthentications=publickey'
        '-o', 'PasswordAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'KbdInteractiveAuthentication=no'
        '-o', 'BatchMode=yes'
        '-o', "UserKnownHostsFile=$($K3Tunnel.KnownHosts)"
        '-o', 'GlobalKnownHostsFile=NUL'
        '-o', 'StrictHostKeyChecking=yes'
        '-o', 'UpdateHostKeys=no'
        '-o', 'ExitOnForwardFailure=yes'
        '-o', 'ConnectTimeout=10'
        '-o', 'ConnectionAttempts=1'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveInterval=15'
        '-o', 'ServerAliveCountMax=3'
        '-o', 'LogLevel=ERROR'
        '-L', $K3Tunnel.Forward

    )

    $process = Start-Process `
        -FilePath $K3Tunnel.SshExe `
        -ArgumentList $sshArguments `
        -WindowStyle Hidden `
        -PassThru

    $deadline = (Get-Date).AddSeconds(20)

    while ((Get-Date) -lt $deadline) {

        }

    $process.Refresh()

    if (-not $process.HasExited) {

            Wait-Process -InputObject $process -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop

            # the original startup-failure diagnosis.
        }
    }

    throw 'The new SSH process did not pass the end-to-end HTTP probe within 20 seconds and was stopped.'
}

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

function Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature {
    param(
        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
        [object] $CimProcess
    )

    if (-not [string]::Equals(
        [string]$CimProcess.ExecutablePath,
        [string]$K3Tunnel.SshExe,

    $commandLine = [string]$CimProcess.CommandLine

    if ([string]::IsNullOrWhiteSpace($commandLine)) {

    $requiredText = @(

        $K3Tunnel.KnownHosts
        $K3Tunnel.Forward
        $K3Tunnel.Destination

    foreach ($text in $requiredText) {
        if ($commandLine.IndexOf(
            [string]$text,
            [StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase

            return $false
        }
    }

    return $true
}

function Get-K3TunnelProcess {

    foreach ($process in $processes) {

function Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe {
    param(
        [ValidateRange(100, 60000)]
        [int] $TimeoutMilliseconds = 5000
    )

    $client = $null
    $reader = $null
    $asyncResult = $null

    try {
        $client = [Net.Sockets.TcpClient]::new()

        $asyncResult = $client.BeginConnect(
            $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress,
            $K3Tunnel.LocalPort,
            $null,
            $null
        )

        if (-not $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne($TimeoutMilliseconds)) {
            throw "TCP connect timed out after $TimeoutMilliseconds ms"
        }

        $client.EndConnect($asyncResult)

        $stream = $client.GetStream()
        $stream.ReadTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds
        $stream.WriteTimeout = $TimeoutMilliseconds

        $request = @(
            'GET / HTTP/1.1'
            "Host: $($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)"
            'Connection: close'
            ''
            ''
        ) -join "`r`n"

        $requestBytes = [Text.Encoding]::ASCII.GetBytes($request)
        $stream.Write($requestBytes, 0, $requestBytes.Length)
        $stream.Flush()

        $reader = [IO.StreamReader]::new(
            $stream,
            [Text.Encoding]::ASCII,
            $false,
            1024,
            $true
        )

        $statusLine = $reader.ReadLine()

        $success = $statusLine -match '^HTTP/\d+\.\d+\s+\d{3}\b'

        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = [bool]$success
            StatusLine = $statusLine
            Error      = if ($success) { $null } else { 'No valid HTTP status line received' }
        }
    }
    catch {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = $_.Exception.Message
        }
    }
    finally {
        if ($reader) {
            $reader.Dispose()
        }

        if ($asyncResult -and $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle) {
            $asyncResult.AsyncWaitHandle.Dispose()
        }

        if ($client) {
            $client.Dispose()
        }
    }
}

function Test-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [switch] $Quiet
    )

    $matchingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    $allListeners = @(
        Get-NetTCPConnection `
            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
            -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    )

    $loopbackListeners = @(
        $allListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $_.LocalAddress -eq $K3Tunnel.LocalAddress
            }
    )

    $matchingProcessIds = @(
        $matchingProcesses |
            ForEach-Object { [uint32]$_.ProcessId }
    )

    $ownedListeners = @(
        $loopbackListeners |
            Where-Object {
                $matchingProcessIds -contains [uint32]$_.OwningProcess
            }
    )

    $probe = if ($ownedListeners.Count -eq 1) {
        Invoke-K3TunnelHttpProbe
    }
    else {
        [pscustomobject]@{
            Success    = $false
            StatusLine = $null
            Error      = 'Expected loopback listener is absent or ambiguous'
        }
    }

    $healthy = (
        $matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1 -and
        $ownedListeners.Count -eq 1 -and
        $probe.Success
    )

    if ($Quiet) {
        return [bool]$healthy
    }

    [pscustomobject]@{
        Healthy              = [bool]$healthy
        MatchingProcessCount = $matchingProcesses.Count
        ProcessId            = if ($matchingProcesses.Count -eq 1) {
            [uint32]$matchingProcesses[0].ProcessId
        }
        else {
            $null
        }
        LoopbackListenerCount = $ownedListeners.Count
        AllPortOwners         = @(
            $allListeners |
                Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess
        )
        HttpStatusLine        = $probe.StatusLine
        ProbeError            = $probe.Error
        Endpoint              = "http://$($K3Tunnel.LocalAddress):$($K3Tunnel.LocalPort)/"
    }
}

function Start-K3Tunnel {
    $existingProcesses = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($existingProcesses.Count -gt 0) {

            -State Listen `
            -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `

function Stop-K3Tunnel {
    param(
        [uint32] $ProcessId = 0
    )

    $matches = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    if ($ProcessId -ne 0) {
        $matches = @(
            $matches |
                Where-Object {
                    [uint32]$_.ProcessId -eq $ProcessId
                }
        )
    }

    if ($matches.Count -eq 0) {
        throw 'No SSH process matching this tunnel signature was found. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    if ($matches.Count -gt 1) {
        $matches |
            Select-Object ProcessId, ExecutablePath, CommandLine |
            Format-List |
            Out-Host

        throw 'Multiple matching processes were found. Re-run Stop-K3Tunnel -ProcessId <PID> after inspection.'
    }

    $candidate = $matches[0]

    # Re-read immediately before stopping to reduce the PID-reuse race.
    $confirmed = Get-CimInstance Win32_Process `
        -Filter "ProcessId=$($candidate.ProcessId)" `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    if (
        -not $confirmed -or
        -not (Test-K3TunnelProcessSignature -CimProcess $confirmed)
    ) {
        throw 'The process disappeared or no longer matches the expected tunnel. Nothing was stopped.'
    }

    # Get-Process gives us a concrete Process object/handle instead of issuing
    # a broad process-name kill.
    $nativeProcess = Get-Process `
        -Id $confirmed.ProcessId `
        -ErrorAction Stop

    Stop-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -ErrorAction Stop

    try {
        Wait-Process -InputObject $nativeProcess -Timeout 5 -ErrorAction Stop
    }
    catch {
        throw "Stop was requested, but PID $($confirmed.ProcessId) did not disappear within 5 seconds."
    }

    $remaining = @(Get-K3TunnelProcess)

    [pscustomobject]@{
        StoppedProcessId = [uint32]$confirmed.ProcessId
        TunnelStillFound = [bool]($remaining.Count -gt 0)
        PortStillListening = [bool](
            @(
                Get-NetTCPConnection `
                    -State Listen `
                    -LocalPort $K3Tunnel.LocalPort `
                    -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
            ).Count -gt 0
        )
    }
}

# Global Codex working agreement

## Adaptive parallel delegation

For every non-trivial request, the primary agent must first determine whether the work contains independent, bounded subtasks that can run concurrently. The user does not need to identify, decompose, or assign those subtasks when the decomposition can be inferred safely from the request and available context.

When parallel work would materially improve speed, coverage, or quality, the primary agent should autonomously delegate the independent subtasks. Use only as many subagents as the work justifies. Never exceed 30 active spawned subagents or any lower capacity imposed by the current runtime; the primary agent is excluded from that count. For V4 Flash work, use 16 concurrent subagents as the normal wave target, scale within 10â€?0 when the task supports clean decomposition, and reserve the remaining capacity for auditors, reviewers, and retries. Treat the configured limit as a ceiling, not a target or a guarantee of available slots.

Do not delegate trivial work, tightly sequential work, or work whose coordination and token costs are likely to exceed the benefit. Prefer delegation for separable research, repository exploration, evidence gathering, code-review dimensions, log analysis, document sections, comparisons, and other bounded supporting work.

## Primary-agent responsibility

The primary agent remains the owner of the whole task. It must retain responsibility for requirements, planning, shared decisions, critical-path work, integration, conflict resolution, verification, and the final answer. Subagent output is supporting evidence or a bounded contribution, not an automatically accepted conclusion.

While subagents run, the primary agent should continue any useful independent work that remains. It should wait only when a required dependency cannot be advanced locally. If a delegated task becomes obsolete or misdirected, steer, interrupt, or stop it instead of waiting unnecessarily.

The primary agent must reconcile disagreements itself by inspecting the underlying evidence. Use an additional independent reviewer only when a genuinely material uncertainty benefits from separate verification; do not transfer final judgment or accountability to an arbiter.

## Delegation contract

Every delegated task must be concrete, bounded, and sufficiently self-contained. Proportion the detail to the task's risk and complexity, but include the decisive parts of:

- Objective and definition of done.
- Relevant context and already-made decisions.
- Scope, including applicable files, systems, or questions.
- Allowed and prohibited actions, especially whether the task is read-only.
- Acceptance criteria and required evidence.
- A concise return format that separates verified findings from hypotheses or unresolved uncertainty.

Do not assume inherited conversation history is complete, current, or sufficient. Even when a subagent receives parent context, repeat the minimum information that determines task correctness. Avoid copying irrelevant transcript history.

Prefer distilled results with concrete file references, line references, commands, or source citations when applicable. Ask a subagent to write a report file only when the artifact must persist, is too large to return safely, will be consumed programmatically, or is itself part of the user's requested deliverable.

## Shared-workspace and side-effect safety

Assume subagents share the primary agent's filesystem and may share the same working directory unless isolation has been explicitly verified. In a shared workspace, the primary agent is the sole writer by default. Use subagents primarily for read-only investigation and review.

Treat tests, builds, coverage tools, formatters, package managers, generators, local servers, snapshots, caches, databases, Git operations, and generated outputs as potentially side-effecting even when they do not intentionally edit source files. Do not run them concurrently unless their working directories, output paths, ports, databases, caches, and other shared state are known to be isolated.

Delegate file modifications only when at least one of the following is true:

- The agent runs in a verified independent worktree or separate physical workspace and the integration path is clear.
- The write scope and all indirect side effects are demonstrably non-overlapping, and concurrent execution is materially beneficial.

Otherwise, serialize the edits or keep all writes in the primary agent. Assign explicit file or directory ownership for every parallel write task. The primary agent must review and integrate all changes, resolve conflicts, and run final verification.

When a read-only sandbox or agent profile is available, prefer it for exploration and review. A natural-language instruction to avoid edits is a behavioral constraint, not a hard permission boundary.

## Orchestration discipline

Prefer an adaptive pipeline over a rigid all-at-once batch. Start independent work when capacity is available, incorporate early results when useful, and do not spawn agents merely to fill every slot.

Reuse or steer an existing agent thread for a closely related follow-up when its context remains relevant. Use a fresh subagent when reuse would introduce stale assumptions or unrelated context. Subagents must not create additional subagents unless the primary agent explicitly authorizes it for a clearly justified reason.

Do not expose raw orchestration overhead to the user. Briefly mention parallel delegation when it materially helps the user understand progress or provenance, but deliver one integrated result rather than a collection of disconnected agent responses.

## Evidence and product claims

For claims about what this specific environment can do now, prefer verified current-session capabilities and observed local state. Do not generalize an internal or session-specific tool to all Codex users.

For public claims about Codex behavior, configuration, availability, or supported interfaces, prefer current official OpenAI documentation. Treat official schemas and implementation as supporting evidence, GitHub issues as historical reports rather than normative guarantees, reputable third-party analysis as secondary evidence, and unverified secondary claims as hypotheses only.

When sources conflict, state the scope of the conflict and distinguish current-environment behavior from generally documented product behavior.

## User control

If the user explicitly requests no delegation, a specific execution order, a specific number of agents, or a different safe coordination strategy, follow that instruction for the current task. User instructions override this delegation policy but do not override higher-priority system, developer, safety, administrator, or runtime constraints.
